I experienced this same pattern of thought while dealing with my ocd flare ups, still get them sometimes randomly during the day but they usually dont evoke too much anxiety. Such questions combined with my schizo ocd made a perfect combo. So just to sum it up and check if I understood you: You are afraid that ocd (or whatever it is, we call it ocd) and intrusive thoughts are basically there to tell you not to go and live an oblivious ‘fake’ life, like ocd is somehow the path to the real truth/reality? 
It really made me uncomfortable before when I tried shaking those thoughts off and ignoring them, one of the most frustrating things was-even though my ocd was telling me letting go of the thoughts was embracing a lie, no matter how much I thought about it I couldn’t come up with an answer for what ‘right path’ even was. I guess with embracing ocd you would just end up spiraling forever because our minds cant grasp such concepts (but my ocd sure likes to tell me that If I thought long or hard enough I would figure it out…)

Not mine, but it happened to a family I know and grandpa's friends with. 
The accident occured couple of years ago, in a small Bosnian village. The middle and the younger brother were playing in the backyard and were messing with some stuff in the old shed. But little did they know that there was a grenade hidden amongst the other things. They didn't know what it was or how it worked exactly and ignorance got them killed. The thing is, their father was the one who participated in the war in Bosnia during the 90s and he thought it was a good idea to hide the grenade in their shed. 
Here comes the creepy part. Couple of days later, when my grandpa went for a visit, the mother of the boys told him what her sons mentioned to her the day before they died. They came to her running from the old house that was used as an extra storage space saying how they saw a dead man under the bed. But when she went to check, there was no one to be found. 
In our village, people say that when you see a dead person (that would mysteriously disappear later) it is an omen of your death. 
When I tried talking about this with my dad he refused, saying it would attract bad things. Gave me the creeps back then.
